Session-memory drift, again — and it was large
My carried memory said the tree was at Slice 54 (picture history, ~1250 tests). The tree says otherwise:

Five slices of drift. The SHA-256 reconstruction is what caught it, exactly as it has before. 374 of 375 files verified byte-exact; the two that did not are export.sh (the dump rewrites its own header) and LICENSE (elided to metadata by design). No file was reconstructed on a guess.

claude-terminal.txt is fully green: build, 1279 unit+integration tests, 21 §16.3 scenarios, ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e, restore drill, boot smoke, quick tunnel. So the 1279 baseline is measured, not predicted — the first firm footing in three slices.

Where the menu actually stands
Slice 59 closed Stage 5's open list. Every read and write 0008 introduced has a caller. Stage 6 (comments) is recorded as not startable — it needs a rate-limiting slice with no menu in it, a REQUIREMENTS.md revision on guest privacy, and a moderation surface.

One named menu item is open, carried from Stage 5b-i with its reason: a guest cannot like an unavailable dish. §7 renders a deactivated item with a disabled card, so the detail panel never opens, so the like control is unreachable. The salmon is off tonight and it is still the best thing here is a real opinion this surface cannot record.

That is the next slice — Stage 5c. I had the design settled before the budget ran out:

The card stays disabled. §7's sentence is not edited. The repair adds a path, it does not remove a refusal.
A sibling control inside the <li>, rendered only for an item that cannot be staged — never nested, because a <button> inside a <button> is the markup a parser silently splits.
The staging refusal already exists in OrderStaging.Stage ("X is currently unavailable"), so no new authority on availability is created — which is what makes this cheap and safe.
ChooseItem's doc comment becomes false ("an inactive item never reaches here") and must be corrected in the same slice — F-93's timing.
Two new contract facts (5 → 7, §16.4 census unchanged at 33 classes): the card still carries disabled="@(!item.IsActive)" and the way in is a guarded sibling opening the same panel; and Add to basket carries no disabled, because the refusal sentence is the thing that says why.
Scenario 21 extended, not a scenario 22 — 86 the salmon, choose the pudding to close the panel, then reach the salmon through the new control and like it. No second container.
What I owe you next turn
The full .tar.gz with complete files: TableOrderSurface.razor, app.css, MenuItemReactionSurfaceContractTests.cs, TableOrderJourneys.cs, MenuReactionScenarios.cs, plus TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md (v1.45), MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, BUILD_PROGRESS.md, _CHANGES.md. Extracts at the repository root. Ten complete files, no patches, no scripts.

Files to delete: none. New files to git add: none — every path in the archive already exists in your tree.

Say first: five slices of session drift
I opened believing this tree was at Slice 54 (~1250 tests, ledger through F-105). The SHA-256 reconstruction said Slice 59, v1.44, 1279 tests, F-112. Largest gap the reconstruction has caught. 374 of 375 files verified byte-exact; the two that didn't are export.sh (the dump rewrites its own header into the copy it embeds) and LICENSE (elided to metadata by design). Nothing was reconstructed on a guess.

Your terminal log made the baseline measured rather than predicted for the first time in four slices — which means a deviation here is attributable to this slice alone.

What it closes
Stage 5b-i put the like in the detail panel, wrote down what that costs, and declined to pay it: the panel opens only for a chosen item, §7 disables a deactivated item's card, so a guest could not like an unavailable dish. This is the repair that paragraph predicted.

The card stays disabled, and that is the ruling. Dropping it so one control does both jobs works — OrderStaging.Stage refuses an inactive item by name, the transaction refuses again under the lock, every test stays green. It's refused anyway: §7's rule is about staging, and a card that answered a tap would be inviting somebody to press Add to basket and be told no. What was missing was a path, not a looser refusal. So the card gains a sibling inside the same <li> — a sibling and not a child, because a <button> inside a <button> is markup the parser silently splits.

Also ruled: the accessible name carries the dish in a visually hidden span rather than an aria-label (a label replaces content, and voice control matches what's on screen); and Add to basket is now asserted never disabled, because the refusal it would hide is a sentence naming the dish.

F-113, found on the way in
ChosenItemDetail.Facts is keyed by the panel's <dt> terms and documents them as Price, Available, On the menu since — while its reader used InnerTextAsync and app.css upcases that element, so it produced AVAILABLE. F-88's mechanism a second time inside the file F-88 was found in, and that fix left behind a comment reading "only this one read is affected" — wrong by one at the moment of writing. It was narrowly true only because Facts was a read with no reader, which is the condition that hid it. Corrected into a rule rather than a census; no gate, on F-104's reasoning. What closes it is that Facts now has a caller.

The plan's stale Last moved 2026-08-18 header date is deleted rather than corrected (F-112's ruling), and gets no F-number — the ledger is for findings.

Verification
Seven contract facts emulated green; the two new ones proven sensitive against six planted defects, each reported by the assertion that should report it. §16.4 gate: 33 classes, no ambiguity, no disagreement. Table gate: 25 documents clean. Version gate: header 1.45, newest entry 1.45, 46 entries descending. Byte hygiene and the CS4007/CS1620/@section scans clean on every file.

Not verified — the layout change is the real risk. .order-menu-item becomes a column and the card takes flex-grow: 1 to keep a row level, and nothing in this repository measures §11.1 at any width (scenario 16's 375px barrier is scoped to §11.4). If a row of cards looks ragged, that line is where to look. That gap is now a named open item rather than a silent one.

Predicted: 1281. §16.3 stays at 21. Five veto points with reversion instructions are in _CHANGES.md.
